findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence is not corroborated by descendant survival credit: the top-ranked survival_enrichment_z rows (sorted by q) are all null (effect_z near zero, CIs spanning zero, q~0.999, positive_batch_fraction 0.43-0.64), so no landmark coordinate shows a survival/quality advantage at the multiplicity-adjusted level.

The later-label calculation is terminal-credit mining over a 0.0-0.5 learning window with terminal score time 0.99 and state time 1.0, i.e. last-record joint-head credit outside the observed support; it is not a decoded terminal affinity label, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Ancestral coverage is thin and survivor bias is plausible: 349 of 700 batch nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with only 14 complete-survival batches and at most 2 teachers per batch, so survival-conditioned credit is dominated by shallow lineages.

The immediate-selection audit itself is a geometric nearest-teacher comparison, not the score-weighted FLOWR reward or its Jacobian; its own limitations state the nonnegative excess distance is by construction and not a causal affinity effect, and teacher score correlations are observational, not a validated affinity predictor.

Curve support is restricted to 24 selected features under a fidelity rule (relative RMSE <= 0.35, zero strong sign-conflict nodes, quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1) and a selection rule (|integrated z| >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05); the fidelity audit contents are container-summarized and were not read numerically, so per-curve sign changes and rate changes remain unverified here.

hypotheses.direction: downweight selection-only coordinate priorities until survival credit is decoded
hypotheses.falsifier: a landmark feature with q<0.05, |effect_z| materially above zero and positive_batch_fraction >= 0.857
hypotheses.observable: survival_enrichment_z with batch direction fraction for the same landmark features
hypotheses.statement: If a landmark coordinate carried genuine descendant quality credit, its survival_enrichment_z would be nonzero with a consistent batch direction; the observed nulls indicate the immediate-selection signal and survival credit disagree, so direction priorities should not be set from point estimates of selection alone.

hypotheses.direction: descriptive only until per-curve fits are read
hypotheses.falsifier: all selected curves show zero sign changes and constant rate within fit tolerance
hypotheses.observable: sign_changes, first/last rate z and relative_node_RMSE per selected feature
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule could differ from a constant rule only where validated curve fits show sign changes or rate changes within the observed support; this cannot be asserted from the summarized fidelity audit.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record joint-head credit is not final affinity benefit and the immediate-selection vs final-affinity comparison is unavailable.
Survival and turnover tables are diagnostic accounting, not causal selection effects or atom velocities.
The curve_fidelity_audit container was not read numerically, so per-curve sign-change and rate-change comparisons are not established.
No current-study outcome data are available to this role; all statements are observational within the supplied 0.0-0.5 window.
